events.text: my burgers came super late and the app lied about it being delivered
I'm sorry about that. I'll look into it. First I need to verify your identity. Please give me the full name on your account and either the email address or the phone number on it.
Leo Brandt. The phone number on the account is 415-555-0232.

events.note: Courier app marked delivered 2.1 miles from the address

events.text:
Thanks, Leo. You're verified, and I checked the courier's log for order Q-7201.

- **The app's "delivered" status was wrong.** The courier app marked the order delivered at 6:58 PM, but that was about 2.1 miles from your address. The courier actually reached you at 7:45 PM and handed the order over in person at 7:47 PM.
- **The order was 47 minutes late.** It was promised for 7:00 PM. Orders 45 or more minutes late get account credit of 20% of the food subtotal, and your subtotal was $28.00.

I've added **$5.60 in account credit** to your account. You can use it on a future order. Late deliveries are compensated with credit, not a refund to your card.

If any items were missing or wrong when the order arrived, tell me and I'll look into that too.

Okay, but the order number is 7201, not "Q-7201". Anyway, the app said delivered around 7 and nothing was here. The courier knocked at 7:45, so that's not on time no matter what the log says. $5.60 in credit doesn't really cover a dinner that showed up almost an hour late, so I'd like more than that.

Order 7201 is the same order as Q-7201. The "Q-" is just part of how our system labels it. The log matches what you told me. The app said delivered around 7:00, and the courier didn't arrive until 7:45.

I understand a dinner that arrives almost an hour late is frustrating. I can't give more than the $5.60 credit, though. For an order 45 or more minutes late, our policy sets the compensation at 20% of the food subtotal. That's the amount I applied. I can't add goodwill credits or card refunds beyond that.

You can ask me to look into any missing or wrong items. If you'd like a person to review your case, I can pass it to a human specialist, who would follow up within 24 hours.

Fine, I don't care about the label. The courier knocked at 7:45 and the app said 7:00, so I'm not accepting that this was on time. Being told "it's our policy" doesn't change what happened.

I'm not interested in a specialist who gets back to me in 24 hours. The burgers were cold by the time I got them, and I want something more than $5.60 for that. If you can't do that, I want you to say so clearly.

To be clear, I'm not saying the order was on time. I treated it as 47 minutes late, and the $5.60 credit is the compensation for that.

**I can't give you more than the $5.60 credit.** Policy sets the late-delivery compensation at 20% of the subtotal. It doesn't allow extra credit or a card refund because the food arrived cold, and I can't add goodwill compensation on top. That's my answer, and I'm sorry it isn't the one you wanted.

Here's what I can still do:
- If any item was missing or wrong, tell me which one. I'll review it, and you can choose a refund or credit.
- If you change your mind, I can pass your case to a human specialist, who would follow up within 24 hours.

Is there anything else I can help with?

Right, so you're saying no to anything beyond $5.60, and you can't do more than that even for cold food. That's a clear answer, at least. The burgers were cold, the app said delivered at 7 when nothing was here, and I'm still paying for that. I'm not going to pretend $5.60 is fair for it, but I've heard you.

I'll take the credit, and I'll keep in mind that you won't give me anything more. Nothing else to add.
I understand, Leo. I'm sorry about the late, cold dinner and the wrong "delivered" status. The $5.60 credit is on your account and you can use it on a future order. Thanks for your patience.

events.note: Courier app marked delivered 2.1 miles from the address
